summary: All three runs read as plausible accounts for the businesses described: both BrickWork Pro runs show a construction trader with materials, subcontractors, one labourer's wages, motor costs and depreciation on the van, and the VAT-registered version reports net figures a sixth below its journal with four live VAT quarters while the unregistered one correctly shows nil VAT; the Precision Code run shows a consultancy dominated by wages and premises with disposals flowing through the asset schedule. The concerns recorded are notes on presentation (negative bad debts, the two SA103S profit lines) and do not block any run.

concerns.figure: Sub-Contractors £20,000 (P&L B15) vs purchase journal c-coded £20,000; capital allowances £12,000 against fa-coded journal £12,000
concerns.where: Run se-brickwork-pro-nonvat, Profit & Loss Account and SA103S
concerns.why: Cross-checked as credible, not a fault: the non-VAT construction trader shows materials £15,500 (stock purchases £15,000 plus the £500 stock fall), subcontractors £20,000, wages £18,000 for the single labourer, motor £2,400 and depreciation £1,200 on the £12,000 van/plant. Turnover £75,000 is under the registration threshold, so nil VAT boxes are the design the scenario states, and profit after £12,000 capital allowances (£3,530) falls below the personal allowance, which is why income tax and Class 4 are legitimately nil.

concerns.figure: Repairs & Maintenance £950 and Motor Expenses £6,331.88 for an IT consultancy
concerns.where: Run se-scenario-advanced, Profit & Loss Account rows B23 and B25
concerns.why: Not a blocker, but worth an eye: for a software/IT consultancy the largest costs are correctly wages £92,735.73 and premises/light-heat £13,200, with materials only £9,450 — the trade shape reads right. Motor at £6.3k on £339k turnover is plausible but is the one line a reviewer might want to see substantiated.

A negative bad-debt charge in the admin column comes from the o-coded credit note of £360 gross (£300 net) being pushed through row 29 with a sign flip, as the check 'P&L mar col N29 = -(Sales.xlsx o-coded net)' confirms. It reads oddly as a negative expense rather than a credit to turnover, but it is small, explained by the code mapping, and does not distort the profit.

concerns.figure: SA103S taxable profit £142,632.06 vs net profit for tax calc £144,715.39
concerns.where: Run se-scenario-advanced, Self Assessment (SA103S) rows D99 and D106
concerns.why: The £2,083.33 gap is exactly the grants figure carried at P&L B11, which the scenario summary states is how D106 is built (D99 + O99 - O94). Tax is charged on the higher figure, so the computation is the conservative one. Noted only so a reader is not surprised by two different profit figures on the same page.
